title: Thick Pork Chops, Medium Rare (Cook 5, Freeze 4)
description: Reverse-seared thick pork chops, pulled at about 135°F for medium rare. Cook 5, eat 1, freeze 4.

ingredients.note: thawed (move to fridge Fri night; thick chops need about 24 hours)

ingredients.item: salt and your favorite pork rub

steps: Pat the chops very dry. Salt both sides and season. Best if done 30 to 60 min ahead and left uncovered in the fridge.
Preheat oven to 275°F, regular Bake mode. Chops on a rack over a lightly oiled sheet pan.
Bake until the center of the thickest chop reads 120 to 125°F, about 25 to 45 min depending on thickness. Start checking at 20 min.
Heat a skillet over high with the oil until it just starts to smoke. Sear 2 or 3 chops at a time, 60 to 90 seconds per side, until well browned. Add butter at the end for flavor.
Pull at about 135°F. For the 4 going in the freezer, pull them a little lower (about 130°F) since reheating adds a few degrees.
Cool and freeze the other 4: cool on the rack 20 to 30 min, then fridge uncovered until fully cold (about 1 hour). Get them in the fridge within 2 hours of cooking.
Put each chop in its own quart Ziploc freezer bag and squeeze out the air.
Label "Cooked pork chops, Oct 25." Best within 1 month, safe 2 to 3 months.
source: Joe's Meal Pack, Oct 20 to Nov 4, 2026 (built by Thrifty, now kept by Meal Plan), R17
notes:
About 1 hour. Joe likes them medium rare: pull at about 135°F, then rest. (USDA guidance is 145°F with a 3 minute rest.)
Oven-only option: Air Fry mode 400°F preheated, rack over sheet pan, 10 to 16 min, flip halfway, start checking at 8 min. Less even, still good.
Foil removed Oct 25, 2026 (Joe has no foil); per Joe via Meal Plan.

healthy: Thick pork chops give plenty of protein.
Simple pan sear with little added fat.
not_healthy: Pork rub and salt add sodium.
Butter adds a little saturated fat.
